Container.Name: TasmoFleet
Container.Overview: TasmoFleet is a fleet manager for Tasmota devices and an alternative to TasmoAdmin (it imports its device list).[br][br]Highlights:[br]- Fleet overview with live status, bulk commands and a dashboard that lists what needs attention.[br]- Firmware updates over the air with a safe rollout: image header and chip-family checks, one batch at a time, per-device progress.[br]- Policy rules with a command catalogue: define the settings every device should have, see compliance, fix deviations in one go.[br]- Config backups (scheduled or on demand, diff, one-click restore, also onto a replacement device) and snapshots of TasmoFleet's own database.[br]- Notifications by webhook (e.g. Home Assistant) or email when an update finishes or a scheduled backup or snapshot fails.[br]- Per-device stability: restart reasons, boot loops and weak Wi-Fi at a glance.[br][br]MQTT is optional; every feature also works over HTTP alone. Devices fetch firmware over plain HTTP from a dedicated port of this container.[br][br]Settings live in the web UI (System, Settings) after the first sign-in; environment variables are only for bootstrap. The first admin password is written to initial-admin-password in the appdata folder. All variables: https://github.com/nofuturekid/tasmofleet/blob/main/docs/configuration.md[br][br]Pre-1.0: breaking changes are to be expected; read the changes below or the release notes before updating.

Existing containers keep working without any change (unless the UI listen row was deleted, see below), because Unraid keeps your saved values (UI listen :8443 or :8080 is still honoured). To adopt the new layout: Edit the container, delete those three variables, and set the Web UI container port to 8080 (the host port, for example 8443, stays). On br0 or a custom IP there is no port mapping: the container listens on the saved UI listen port (8443 with the template defaults, 8080 in the proxy setup). If you delete UI listen, it listens on 8080 (UI) and 80 (firmware) of its IP, so update bookmarks and the reverse proxy upstream. Two saved combinations change: a container with an 8443:8443 mapping whose UI listen row was deleted from its template (it was :8443 before and is :8080 now) is unreachable on the old port until you set the container port to 8080 (an emptied UI listen field falls back to the template default :8443 and keeps working); and Self-signed TLS true together with Trusted proxies now serves plain HTTP, so point the proxy at http://. Config.Name: Web UI (HTTPS)
Config.Description: Web UI and API (container port 8080; choose the host port). Serves a self-signed certificate by default; behind a reverse proxy (see Trusted proxies) the same port serves plain HTTP.

Config.Name: Firmware server
Config.Description: Device-facing firmware server (plain HTTP; ESP8266 devices cannot use TLS). Tasmota devices download firmware from this port during an update. Choose any free host port that the devices can reach, and enter the resulting http://SERVER-IP:PORT/ URL as the firmware URL on the System settings page. Host port 80 is used by the Unraid web interface.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Database, secret.key, firmware cache and backups. Back it up as a whole: without secret.key the stored device passwords cannot be decrypted. The container runs as UID/GID 65532 (not nobody 99:100): run 'chown -R 65532:65532 /mnt/user/appdata/tasmofleet' once if the folder is not writable.

Config.Name: Public URL
Config.Description: Only behind a reverse proxy or with single sign-on: external URL of the UI, e.g. https://tasmofleet.example.com. Used as OIDC redirect and logout target. Leave empty otherwise.

Config.Name: Trusted proxies
Config.Description: Only behind a reverse proxy: comma separated CIDRs of the proxy, e.g. 192.168.1.10/32. Forwarded headers and header authentication are trusted only from these peers, and the UI port then serves plain HTTP instead of the self-signed HTTPS (the proxy talks http:// to it; the Web UI link above is https). Leave empty otherwise.

Config.Name: Initial admin password
Config.Description: Password of the first local admin ('admin') on a fresh install; it must be changed at the first sign-in. Empty: a random one is written to initial-admin-password in the appdata folder.

Config.Name: Metrics token
Config.Description: Leave empty to set the scrape token on the settings page (System, Metrics); a value here locks it. Bearer token required on /metrics for remote Prometheus scrapers; without any token only local scrapes are answered.

Config.Name: Log level
Config.Description: debug, info, warn or error. Leave empty to choose it on the settings page; a value here locks it. Logs are JSON on stdout.
